headline: US Q3 GDP Revised Upward to 4.3% as Inflation Gauge Hits Three-Year High
summary: US gross domestic product growth in the third quarter was revised upward to an annualized 4.3%, while the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge rose 3.8% year-on-year in October.
why: Upward revisions to economic growth combined with elevated inflation metrics influence Federal Reserve interest rate expectations and monetary policy outlooks.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Strong GDP data and higher inflation gauges shift bond yields and equity valuations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected GDP growth and persistent inflation readings reinforced expectations for higher-for-longer interest rates, impacting financial market pricing.
